To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) peripheral blood mononucleated cells (PBMC) from normal subjects are able to induce the secretion of anti-thyoid microsomal antibody (AMA) in vitro; and (2) the helper function of CD4 cells in AMA induction is impaired in patients with AIT, while the suppressor function of CD8 in AMA induction is relatively intact.

1) normal B cells can produce anti-thyroid antibodies in vitro in the appropriate environment of T cells; and 2) the T cells of patients with autoimmune thyroid diseases are less able to suppress the production of anti-thy-roid antibodies than are those of normal people.

1) normal B lymphocytes can produce autoantibodies when stimulated in vitro with autologous CD8 cells; 2), in the presence of thyroid antigen, CD4 cells are more active in the production of AMA-M-secrets cells in patients with autoimmune thyroid diseases; and 3), this helper activity is due to impaired suppressor activity of CD8 cells in patients with AITDs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the in vitro induction of autoantibody-secreting cells from peripheral blood mononucleated cells from normal subjects and patients with autoimmune thyroid diseases (AITD).
the immunoregulation of autoantibody production in vitro in patients with AITDs.
the immunoregulation of thyroid autoimmunity, which may provide new insights into the etiology of autoimmune diseases in general.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a defect in the immunoregulation of the CD8 cells in AITD.
the helper activity of autologous or heterologous normal CD4 cells to induce AMA-M-secreters in vitro was similar, while that of CD4 cells in patients with AITDs was greater than in normal subjects.
the helper activity of the CD4 cells from AITD patients may be greater than that of CD4 cells of normal subjects in the induction of anti-thyroperoxidase (TPO) and anti-thyroglobulin (Tg) antibodies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the immune system of patients with autoimmune thyroid disorders is not only capable of producing antibodies to the thyroid, but also has a greater capacity than normal to do so.
the induction of autoantibodies by autologous CD8 cells in vitro is not impaired in AITD patients.
the helper activity of thyroid antigen-specific CD4 cells and/or the suppressor activity of CD8 cells in AITD patients is altered compared with that in normal subjects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the helper activity of autologous CD8 cells from AITD patients to induce AMA-M-secreters is significantly less effective than that of normal subjects.
the induction of autoantibodies can be induced by normal CD4 cells, and that this induction is enhanced by the CD4 cells from autoimmune patients.
we were able to induce the secretion of autoantibodies against the thyroid in vitro.
